claim: Presynaptic membrane-remodeling events such as endocytosis require force-generating actin assembly.
source: Synaptic membrane-remodeling events such as endocytosis require force-generating actin assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about synaptic endocytosis.

claim: The endocytic machinery localizes at high concentrations to large areas of the presynaptic membrane.
source: The endocytic machinery that regulates these actin and membrane dynamics localizes at high concentrations to large areas of the presynaptic membrane, but actin assembly and productive endocytosis are far more restricted in space and time.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by imaging data showing broad distribution of PAZ proteins.

claim: Actin assembly and productive endocytosis are far more restricted in space and time than the endocytic machinery.
source: The endocytic machinery that regulates these actin and membrane dynamics localizes at high concentrations to large areas of the presynaptic membrane, but actin assembly and productive endocytosis are far more restricted in space and time.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by quantitative imaging showing discrete actin patches versus broad PAZ protein distribution.

claim: Collective interactions between Nwk/FCHSD2, Dap160/intersectin, and WASp relieve Nwk autoinhibition.
source: We found that collective interactions between the Drosophila endocytic proteins Nwk/FCHSD2, Dap160/intersectin, and WASp relieve Nwk autoinhibition and promote robust membrane-coupled actin assembly in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by in vitro biochemical assays showing enhanced actin assembly.

claim: Collective interactions between Nwk/FCHSD2, Dap160/intersectin, and WASp promote robust membrane-coupled actin assembly in vitro.
source: We found that collective interactions between the Drosophila endocytic proteins Nwk/FCHSD2, Dap160/intersectin, and WASp relieve Nwk autoinhibition and promote robust membrane-coupled actin assembly in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by pyrene-actin assembly assays and droplet assays.

claim: Nwk-Dap160 interactions constrain spurious assembly of WASp-dependent actin structures.
source: Using automated particle tracking to quantify synaptic actin dynamics in vivo, we discovered that Nwk-Dap160 interactions constrain spurious assembly of WASp-dependent actin structures.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by increased patch frequency in nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants.

claim: Nwk-Dap160 interactions promote synaptic endocytosis.
source: These interactions also promote synaptic endocytosis, suggesting that autoinhibition both clamps and primes the synaptic endocytic machinery, thereby constraining actin assembly to drive productive membrane remodeling in response to physiological cues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by FM dye uptake assays showing reduced endocytosis in nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants.

claim: Autoinhibition both clamps and primes the synaptic endocytic machinery.
source: These interactions also promote synaptic endocytosis, suggesting that autoinhibition both clamps and primes the synaptic endocytic machinery, thereby constraining actin assembly to drive productive membrane remodeling in response to physiological cues.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Actin assembly affects synapse morphogenesis at neuronal presynaptic terminals.
source: At neuronal presynaptic terminals, actin assembly affects many physiological processes including synapse morphogenesis, traffic of numerous vesicular cargoes, and synaptic vesicle endocytosis, organization, and mobility (Dillon and Goda, 2005; Nelson et al., 2013; Papandréou and Leterrier, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Actin assembly affects traffic of numerous vesicular cargoes at neuronal presynaptic terminals.
source: At neuronal presynaptic terminals, actin assembly affects many physiological processes including synapse morphogenesis, traffic of numerous vesicular cargoes, and synaptic vesicle endocytosis, organization, and mobility (Dillon and Goda, 2005; Nelson et al., 2013; Papandréou and Leterrier, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Actin assembly affects synaptic vesicle endocytosis, organization, and mobility at neuronal presynaptic terminals.
source: At neuronal presynaptic terminals, actin assembly affects many physiological processes including synapse morphogenesis, traffic of numerous vesicular cargoes, and synaptic vesicle endocytosis, organization, and mobility (Dillon and Goda, 2005; Nelson et al., 2013; Papandréou and Leterrier, 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The molecular mechanisms that control F-actin dynamics in space and time at presynaptic membranes are largely unknown.
source: However, the molecular mechanisms that control F-actin dynamics in space and time at presynaptic membranes are largely unknown.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a knowledge gap.

claim: Presynaptic terminals maintain constitutively high local concentrations of actin-associated endocytic regulatory proteins at synaptic membranes.
source: Presynaptic terminals maintain constitutively high local concentrations of actin-associated endocytic regulatory proteins at synaptic membranes (Reshetniak et al., 2020; Wilhelm et al., 2014), yet only a small fraction of this protein pool is likely to be active at any point in time (in response to vesicle release) and space (at <100-nm-diameter endocytic sites), suggesting that the endocytic machinery is held in an inactive state at synaptic membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Only a small fraction of the endocytic protein pool is likely to be active at any point in time and space.
source: Presynaptic terminals maintain constitutively high local concentrations of actin-associated endocytic regulatory proteins at synaptic membranes (Reshetniak et al., 2020; Wilhelm et al., 2014), yet only a small fraction of this protein pool is likely to be active at any point in time (in response to vesicle release) and space (at <100-nm-diameter endocytic sites), suggesting that the endocytic machinery is held in an inactive state at synaptic membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the literature.

claim: The endocytic machinery is held in an inactive state at synaptic membranes.
source: Presynaptic terminals maintain constitutively high local concentrations of actin-associated endocytic regulatory proteins at synaptic membranes (Reshetniak et al., 2020; Wilhelm et al., 2014), yet only a small fraction of this protein pool is likely to be active at any point in time (in response to vesicle release) and space (at <100-nm-diameter endocytic sites), suggesting that the endocytic machinery is held in an inactive state at synaptic membranes.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from the literature.

claim: Autoinhibition is a property of multiple endocytic proteins.
source: One plausible mechanism to restrict membrane-cytoskeleton remodeling and endocytic activity to specific locations and times may lie in autoinhibition, which is a property of multiple endocytic proteins (Gerth et al., 2017; Kim et al., 2000; Rao et al., 2010; Stanishneva-Konovalova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nervous Wreck (Nwk) is an F-BAR-SH3 protein that regulates synaptic membrane traffic at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction.
source: One example is the F-BAR-SH3 protein Nervous Wreck (Nwk), which regulates synaptic membrane traffic at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ) (Coyle et al., 2004; O'Connor-Giles et al., 2008; Rodal et al., 2008; Rodal et al., 2011; Ukken et al., 2016) and whose mammalian homolog FCHSD2 regulates endocytosis and endocytic traffic in mammalian cells (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018; Xiao and Schmid, 2020; Xiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: FCHSD2 (mammalian homolog of Nwk) regulates endocytosis and endocytic traffic in mammalian cells.
source: One example is the F-BAR-SH3 protein Nervous Wreck (Nwk), which regulates synaptic membrane traffic at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction (NMJ) (Coyle et al., 2004; O'Connor-Giles et al., 2008; Rodal et al., 2008; Rodal et al., 2011; Ukken et al., 2016) and whose mammalian homolog FCHSD2 regulates endocytosis and endocytic traffic in mammalian cells (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018; Xiao and Schmid, 2020; Xiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Nwk/FCHSD2 proteins couple membrane remodeling and WASp-dependent actin polymerization.
source: Nwk/FCHSD2 proteins couple two activities: membrane remodeling and WASp-dependent actin polymerization (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018; Rodal et al., 2008; Stanishneva-Konovalova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intramolecular autoinhibitory interactions between the Nwk F-BAR and its two SH3 domains mutually inhibit both Nwk membrane binding and activation of WASp.
source: Intramolecular autoinhibitory interactions between the Nwk F-BAR and its two SH3 domains mutually inhibit both Nwk membrane binding and activation of WASp (Stanishneva-Konovalova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: The SH3b domain of Nwk continues to restrict SH3a-mediated WASp activation even after Nwk binds membranes.
source: Unlike other F-BAR-SH3 proteins, which are completely released from autoinhibition upon membrane binding (Guerrier et al., 2009; Meinecke et al., 2013; Rao et al., 2010), the SH3b domain of Nwk continues to restrict SH3a-mediated WASp activation even after Nwk binds membranes (Stanishneva-Konovalova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Autoinhibition allows Nwk-WASp to remain inactive even after recruitment to the membrane.
source: This suggests that autoinhibition allows Nwk-WASp to remain inactive even after recruitment to the membrane, thus keeping the endocytic machinery in a primed but inactive state.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from prior work.

claim: Intersectin (Dap160 in Drosophila) is an excellent candidate for release of Nwk autoinhibition at synapses.
source: An excellent candidate for release of Nwk autoinhibition at synapses is the endocytic adaptor intersectin (Dap160 in Drosophila).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a hypothesis.

claim: Intersectin interacts with numerous endocytic proteins to regulate endocytosis in mammalian cells.
source: Intersectin interacts with numerous endocytic proteins to regulate endocytosis in mammalian cells (Henne et al., 2010; Okamoto et al., 1999; Praefcke et al., 2004; Pucharcos et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 2006; Sengar et al., 1999; Teckchandani et al., 2012) and has been implicated in several steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle (Evergren et al., 2007; Gerth et al., 2017; Jäpel et al., 2020; Pechstein et al., 2010; Pechstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intersectin has been implicated in several steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle.
source: Intersectin interacts with numerous endocytic proteins to regulate endocytosis in mammalian cells (Henne et al., 2010; Okamoto et al., 1999; Praefcke et al., 2004; Pucharcos et al., 2000; Schmid et al., 2006; Sengar et al., 1999; Teckchandani et al., 2012) and has been implicated in several steps of the synaptic vesicle cycle (Evergren et al., 2007; Gerth et al., 2017; Jäpel et al., 2020; Pechstein et al., 2010; Pechstein et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intersectin recruits the Nwk homolog FCHSD2 to sites of endocytosis.
source: Of particular note, intersectin recruits the Nwk homolog FCHSD2 to sites of endocytosis (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018), though it is not yet known how this affects FCHSD2 autoinhibition.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a supporting citation.

claim: Dap160 interacts with WASp, Nwk, and other membrane-remodeling proteins via its four SH3 domains.
source: In Drosophila, Dap160 interacts with WASp, Nwk, and other membrane-remodeling proteins via its four SH3 domains (SH3AD), and regulates the levels and localization of many of these proteins, including Nwk (Koh et al., 2004; Marie et al., 2004; Roos and Kelly, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Dap160 regulates the levels and localization of many membrane-remodeling proteins, including Nwk.
source: In Drosophila, Dap160 interacts with WASp, Nwk, and other membrane-remodeling proteins via its four SH3 domains (SH3AD), and regulates the levels and localization of many of these proteins, including Nwk (Koh et al., 2004; Marie et al., 2004; Roos and Kelly, 1998).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: dap160 mutant phenotypes overlap with those of Nwk and WASp mutants, including impaired synaptic vesicle cycling and synaptic overgrowth.
source: Further, dap160 mutant phenotypes overlap with those of Nwk and WASp mutants, including impaired synaptic vesicle cycling and synaptic overgrowth (Coyle et al., 2004; Khuong et al., 2010; Koh et al., 2004; Marie et al., 2004; Winther et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Intersectin and Dap160 shift localization from synaptic vesicle pools to the plasma membrane in response to synaptic activity.
source: Finally, intersectin and Dap160 shift localization from synaptic vesicle pools to the plasma membrane in response to synaptic activity (Evergren et al., 2007; Gerth et al., 2017; Winther et al., 2015), suggesting that Dap160 may provide the spatiotemporal link between salient physiological triggers and Nwk/WASp activation.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: Actin assembly is required for synaptic vesicle endocytosis at the Drosophila NMJ.
source: To overcome this barrier, we quantified discrete actin assembly events at the Drosophila NMJ as a proxy for productive endocytosis, as actin assembly is both a primary target of the endocytic apparatus under investigation and is required for synaptic vesicle endocytosis in all forms, including at the Drosophila NMJ (Kononenko et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2010; Wu et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with supporting citations.

claim: The predominant structures labeled by actin markers were transient patches at the presynaptic membrane.
source: The predominant structures labeled by these markers were transient patches at the presynaptic membrane (Video 1, Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A), as has been previously observed (Nunes et al., 2006; Pawson et al., 2008; Piccioli and Littleton, 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by imaging data in Figure 1A and Video 1.

claim: GMA patches exhibit an average frequency of 1.2 patches/10 μm2/min at 0.25 Hz imaging.
source: We first imaged at 0.25 Hz and measured an average of 1.2 GMA patches/10 μm2/min, exhibiting a mean duration of 48.0 s ± 45.6 s, with an average relative amplitude of 68 ± 32% ((Imax-Imin)/Imean) (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1C.

claim: GMA patches exhibit a mean duration of 48.0 s ± 45.6 s at 0.25 Hz imaging.
source: We first imaged at 0.25 Hz and measured an average of 1.2 GMA patches/10 μm2/min, exhibiting a mean duration of 48.0 s ± 45.6 s, with an average relative amplitude of 68 ± 32% ((Imax-Imin)/Imean) (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1D.

claim: GMA patches exhibit an average relative amplitude of 68 ± 32%.
source: We first imaged at 0.25 Hz and measured an average of 1.2 GMA patches/10 μm2/min, exhibiting a mean duration of 48.0 s ± 45.6 s, with an average relative amplitude of 68 ± 32% ((Imax-Imin)/Imean) (Figure 1B–D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1B.

claim: GFP::actin and Lifeact::Ruby show very similar dynamics to GMA.
source: Quantification of GFP::actin and Lifeact::Ruby showed very similar dynamics to GMA, suggesting that these measurements robustly reflect the underlying actin dynamics and not the specific properties of a particular probe.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1B-D.

claim: Imaging at 1 Hz identified a larger population of short-duration patches with an average duration of ~16 +/- 20 s.
source: To address this, we also performed imaging at 1 Hz, which could not capture the entire lifetime distribution due to photobleaching but was able to identify a larger population of short-duration patches (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B) with an average duration of ~16 +/- 20 s.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by quantification in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Patch frequency is estimated to be between 2.8 and 10.3 events/10 µm2/min.
source: Given this range of measurements at different sampling frequencies and the efficiency of our automated detection, we estimate that patch frequency is between 2.8 and 10.3 events/10 µm2/min (see 'Materials and methods' for calculations), on par with the expected frequency of endocytic events, and with a similar albeit broader distribution of durations compared to yeast (15 s; Berro and Pollard, 2014) and mammalian cells (~40 s; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results based on calculations from imaging data at different frequencies.

claim: Actin patches colocalize extensively with Arp3::GFP (Pearson coefficient 0.70).
source: We next examined the molecular determinants of synaptic actin patch assembly. Patches strongly co-labeled with Arp3::GFP (Pearson coefficient 0.70), significantly higher than the active zone marker Bruchpilot (BRP), which served as a punctate and membrane-localized negative control (Figure 1E–F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization analysis in Figure 1E-F.

claim: Synaptic actin patches are predominantly composed of branched F-actin.
source: These data suggest that actin patches are predominantly composed of branched F-actin, similar to sites of endocytosis in other cell types (Akamatsu et al., 2020; Collins et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from Arp3 colocalization data.

claim: WASp is required to initiate assembly of presynaptic actin patches.
source: Both genomic and RNAi manipulations significantly reduced the number of actin patches, while genomic mutants also skewed the distribution of patch durations toward both shorter and longer events (Figure 1I). These differences could reflect variable loss of function between the RNAi and mutant, or identify separable presynaptic autonomous (patch frequency) vs non-autonomous (patch duration) effects of WASp. Overall, these data clearly indicate that WASp is autonomously required in neurons to initiate assembly of presynaptic actin patches, similar to its involvement in endocytosis in yeast, mammalian non-neuronal cells, and in the NMJ (Hussain et al., 2001; Kessels and Qualmann, 2004; Khuong et al., 2010; Madania et al., 1999).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by patch frequency data in Figure 1H and Figure 1—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Nwk and Dap160 localize to a membrane-proximal mesh that surrounds active zones.
source: Consistent with these prior descriptions, we observed by structured illumination microscopy (SIM) that the PAZ proteins Nwk and Dap160 localize to a membrane-proximal mesh that surrounds active zones, which were labeled with BRP (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by SIM imaging in Figure 2A.

claim: GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with presynaptic WASp (Pearson's coefficient 0.38).
source: We then compared the localization of PAZ proteins to F-actin patches at the NMJ. As expected, actin patches were much sparser than the endocytic machinery, and GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with each of the presynaptic WASp, Nwk, and Dap160 (Figure 2C–F; Pearson's coefficients of 0.38, 0.38, and 0.36, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization analysis in Figure 2D.

claim: GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with Nwk (Pearson's coefficient 0.38).
source: We then compared the localization of PAZ proteins to F-actin patches at the NMJ. As expected, actin patches were much sparser than the endocytic machinery, and GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with each of the presynaptic WASp, Nwk, and Dap160 (Figure 2C–F; Pearson's coefficients of 0.38, 0.38, and 0.36, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization analysis in Figure 2D.

claim: GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with Dap160 (Pearson's coefficient 0.36).
source: We then compared the localization of PAZ proteins to F-actin patches at the NMJ. As expected, actin patches were much sparser than the endocytic machinery, and GMA-labeled patches only partially overlapped with each of the presynaptic WASp, Nwk, and Dap160 (Figure 2C–F; Pearson's coefficients of 0.38, 0.38, and 0.36, respectively).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization analysis in Figure 2F.

claim: Actin assembly is much sparser both spatially and temporally at the NMJ compared to the actin regulatory machinery.
source: These data confirm that, in sharp contrast to the actin regulatory machinery, which localizes broadly across the PAZ, actin assembly itself is much sparser both spatially and temporally at the NMJ.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the colocalization data.

claim: Purified Dap160 SH3C-containing protein fragments directly interact with NwkSH3b.
source: To determine if and how the candidate activator Dap160 might relieve Nwk autoinhibition, we first mapped their specific interaction domains using glutathione-S-transferase (GST) pulldown assays and found that purified Dap160 SH3C-containing protein fragments (SH3C, SH3CD, or SH3ABCD) directly interact with NwkSH3b, while SH3D alone does not (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1; see Figure 3—figure supplement 2A for details of constructs used).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GST pulldown data in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Dap160 SH3C, SH3D, and SH3CD domain fragments each interact with the isolated Nwk F-BAR domain.
source: Unexpectedly, Dap160 SH3C, SH3D, and SH3CD domain fragments also, each, interact with the isolated Nwk F-BAR domain (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GST pulldown data in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Dap160-NwkF-BAR interactions are mediated by electrostatic interactions.
source: Dap160-NwkF-BAR interactions were progressively eliminated by increasing salt, suggesting they are mediated by electrostatic interactions.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by salt sensitivity data in Figure 3B.

claim: Dap160SH3CD-Nwk interactions are maintained at high salt, suggesting they are mediated primarily by hydrophobic interactions.
source: By contrast, Dap160SH3CD-Nwk interactions were maintained (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C), suggesting that the SH3-SH3 interaction is mediated primarily by hydrophobic interactions, consistent with their mammalian homologs (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018; see summary of interactions in Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by salt sensitivity data in Figure 3B.

claim: Truncation of Dap160SH3CD decreased the levels of Nwk in synaptic boutons similarly to Dap160 knockdown.
source: Finally, we found that truncation of Dap160SH3CD decreased the levels of Nwk in synaptic boutons similarly to Dap160 knockdown (Figure 3D, Figure 3—figure supplement 2B–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by imaging data in Figure 3D.

claim: Dap160ΔSH3CD exhibited reduced colocalization with Nwk compared to wild-type Dap160.
source: Dap160ΔSH3CD also exhibited reduced colocalization with Nwk compared to wild-type Dap160 (Figure 3E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2C), further supporting an in vivo requirement for this interaction.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization data in Figure 3E.

claim: The combination of Nwk and Dap160SH3CD enhances WASp-Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly.
source: At moderate Nwk-Dap160 concentrations (500 nM and 2 µm, respectively), Nwk and Dap160SH3CD significantly enhanced the rate of WASp-Arp2/3-mediated actin assembly compared to Nwk plus WASp alone (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by pyrene-actin assembly data in Figure 4A.

claim: Dap160SH3CD has no effect on WASp-Arp2/3 in the absence of Nwk.
source: This effect is through Nwk, as Dap160SH3CD had no effect on WASp-Arp2/3 in the absence of Nwk.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by pyrene-actin assembly data in Figure 4A.

claim: Dap160 enhancement of Nwk-WASp actin assembly requires the Dap160SH3D domain.
source: Further, Dap160 enhancement of Nwk-WASp actin assembly required the Dap160SH3D domain, further showing that the specific Dap160SH3D-NwkF-BAR interaction relieves functional Nwk autoinhibition in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by pyrene-actin assembly data in Figure 4A.

claim: PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes synergistically activate WASp-mediated actin assembly in concert with Dap160 and Nwk.
source: Indeed, PI(4,5)P2-containing liposomes synergistically activated WASp-mediated actin assembly in concert with Dap160 and Nwk.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by pyrene-actin assembly data in Figure 4B.

claim: Neither Nwk, PI(4,5)P2, nor Nwk + PI(4,5)P2 on their own are sufficient to activate WASp above baseline.
source: By contrast, neither Nwk, PI(4,5)P2, nor Nwk + PI(4,5)P2 on their own were sufficient to activate WASp above baseline (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by pyrene-actin assembly data in Figure 4B.

claim: Coordinated interactions among Nwk, Dap160, and WASp direct actin assembly to the lipid interface in droplet assays.
source: In this assay, we found that coordinated interactions among Nwk, Dap160, and WASp directed actin assembly to the lipid interface.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by droplet assay imaging in Figure 4C.

claim: Substitution of Nwk lacking its autoinhibitory and Dap160-interacting SH3b domain (NwkΔSH3b) causes actin to assemble as free-floating asters.
source: By contrast, substitution of Nwk lacking its autoinhibitory and Dap160-interacting SH3b domain (NwkΔSH3b) caused actin to assemble as free-floating asters (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by droplet assay imaging in Figure 4C.

claim: Dap160SH3CD enhances Nwk membrane binding in a dose-dependent fashion.
source: We found that Dap160SH3CD enhanced Nwk membrane binding in a dose-dependent fashion (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5A.

claim: Dap160SH3CD significantly enhances Nwk membrane binding at both 5 and 10%, but not at 2.5% PI(4,5)P2.
source: This effect depended on membrane charge, as Dap160SH3CD significantly enhanced Nwk membrane binding at both 5 and 10%, but not at 2.5% PI(4,5)P2 (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5B.

claim: Only at 10% PI(4,5)P2 did Dap160SH3CD promote Nwk membrane binding to the same extent as the completely uninhibited NwkFBAR domain alone.
source: Only at 10% PI(4,5)P2 did Dap160SH3CD promote Nwk membrane binding to the same extent as the completely uninhibited NwkFBAR domain alone, suggesting that membrane charge and intermolecular interactions with Dap160 together tune Nwk membrane recruitment.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5B.

claim: Dap160SH3C alone is unable to promote membrane binding by Nwk.
source: Indeed, this effect required the full Dap160SH3CD-NwkSH3b interaction: Dap160SH3C alone was unable to promote membrane binding by Nwk, and Dap160SH3CD did not enhance membrane binding of Nwk lacking its Dap160-interacting SH3b domain (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The addition of Dap160SH3CD and WASp together enhances Nwk membrane association to the level of the isolated F-BAR domain.
source: Indeed, the addition of Dap160SH3CD and WASp together enhanced Nwk membrane association to the level of the isolated F-BAR domain (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5C.

claim: Coordinated binding of all three components (Nwk, Dap160, WASp) results in significantly enriched membrane association of both WASp and Dap160.
source: Moreover, coordinated binding of all three components resulted in significantly enriched membrane association of both WASp and Dap160 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by liposome cosedimentation data in Figure 5C.

claim: Addition of Dap160 and WASp does not change the nature of membrane deformations generated by Nwk.
source: Notably, addition of Dap160 and WASp did not change the nature of membrane deformations generated by Nwk (scalloped and pinched membranes; Becalska et al., 2013), suggesting that Dap160 and WASp together potentiate rather than alter the inherent activity of Nwk (Figure 5—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by GUV imaging in Figure 5—figure supplement 1D.

claim: Knockdown of Dap160 by RNAi leads to a striking loss of endogenously tagged Nwk::GFP from synaptic membranes.
source: Knockdown of Dap160 by RNAi (Figure 5E, Figure 3—figure supplement 2D) led to a striking loss of endogenously tagged Nwk::GFP from synaptic membranes (note strong peripheral labeling in control bouton cross-sections; Figure 5E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by imaging data in Figure 5E.

claim: Dap160 knockdown significantly increases the rate of recovery of Nwk::GFP after photobleaching.
source: Further, Dap160 knockdown significantly increased the rate of recovery of Nwk::GFP after photobleaching, consistent with a shift in localization from membrane-bound to cytosolic (Figure 5F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FRAP data in Figure 5F.

claim: Both nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants significantly increase patch frequency.
source: We found that both nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants significantly increased patch frequency (Figure 6B,E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1), supporting a clamp function for these proteins.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by patch frequency data in Figure 6B and 6E.

claim: nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants do not show a difference in the distribution of patch lifetimes.
source: We did not detect a difference in the distribution of patch lifetimes, suggesting that it is the frequency of events, and not their duration per se, that changes (Figure 6C,F).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by patch duration data in Figure 6C and 6F.

claim: Both Dap160ΔSH3D and Dap160ΔSH3CD truncations rescue satellite bouton numbers to wild-type levels.
source: Surprisingly, we found that both Dap160ΔSH3D and Dap160ΔSH3CD truncations rescued satellite bouton numbers to wild-type levels (Figure 7—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by satellite bouton quantification in Figure 7—figure supplement 2.

claim: Synaptic vesicle and growth factor endocytosis are mechanistically separable.
source: These data indicate that synaptic vesicle and growth factor endocytosis are mechanistically separable, and suggest that actin dynamics phenotypes in the Dap160ΔSH3CD mutant are not associated with synaptic growth regulation.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the satellite bouton rescue data.

claim: nwk1/2 null mutants lead to a 34% decrease in FM4-64fx uptake compared to controls.
source: nwk1/2 null mutants led to a 34% decrease in FM4-64fx uptake compared to controls (Figure 7F–G), an intermediate phenotype compared to dominant negative dynamin in shiTS1 mutants (72% decrease).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FM dye uptake data in Figure 7F-G.

claim: Expression of Dap160ΔSH3CD in dap160 null mutants significantly diminishes FM dye uptake to a similar extent as loss of nwk (27% reduction).
source: Indeed, we found that expression of Dap160ΔSH3CD in dap160 null mutants also significantly diminished FM dye uptake to a similar extent as loss of nwk (27% reduction; Figure 7H–I).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FM dye uptake data in Figure 7H-I.

claim: Loss of the Dap160SH3D domain alone causes no defects in FM uptake.
source: By contrast, loss of the Dap160SH3D domain alone caused no defects in FM uptake, consistent with the lack of effect of this mutation on Nwk accumulation and localization (Figure 3D–E), suggesting that this interaction, though required in vitro, may be compensated by additional factors in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FM dye uptake data in Figure 7H-I.

claim: Both nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants unload FM dye to the same extent as controls.
source: Both nwk and Dap160ΔSH3CD mutants unloaded FM dye to the same extent as controls, suggesting that diminished endocytosis is a direct phenotype, and not secondary to exocytic deficits (Figure 7—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by FM dye unloading data in Figure 7—figure supplement 3.

claim: Spurious actin assembly events in nwk and dap160 mutants are likely to be unproductive for normal endocytosis.
source: Importantly, these data indicate that spurious actin assembly events in nwk and dap160 mutants are likely to be unproductive for normal endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results as an inference from the combined actin dynamics and FM dye uptake data.

claim: Normal synaptic actin patches represent active endocytic events.
source: Overall, our data support the hypothesis that normal synaptic actin patches represent active endocytic events and indicate that Dap160-Nwk regulation of actin patch dynamics is functionally required for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from multiple lines of evidence.

claim: Dap160-Nwk regulation of actin patch dynamics is functionally required for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
source: Overall, our data support the hypothesis that normal synaptic actin patches represent active endocytic events and indicate that Dap160-Nwk regulation of actin patch dynamics is functionally required for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the results as a conclusion from the FM dye uptake and actin dynamics data.

claim: Actin patches colocalize with the endocytic adaptor Clc.
source: A significant proportion of endogenously labeled AP2 at the NMJ is likely associated with the closely apposed postsynaptic membrane, which accounts for its slightly lower correlation coefficient with Lifeact::Ruby. Considering that the rates of exo/endocytosis at this synapse at rest are relatively low (see above), these observations suggest that like other PAZ endocytic proteins, a large pool of membrane-localized clathrin coat and adaptor proteins are not actively engaged in endocytosis. Despite these caveats, we found that actin significantly colocalized with both Clc (Figure 7C) and AP2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), consistent with a role in endocytosis for these actin-enriched sites.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization data in Figure 7C.

claim: Actin patches colocalize with the endocytic adaptor AP2.
source: Despite these caveats, we found that actin significantly colocalized with both Clc (Figure 7C) and AP2 (Figure 7—figure supplement 1C), consistent with a role in endocytosis for these actin-enriched sites.
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by colocalization data in Figure 7—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Shi disruption decreases the frequency of actin patch dynamics.
source: To more rigorously and functionally test the hypothesis that actin patches are endocytic, we acutely disrupted endocytic dynamics using the temperature-sensitive dominant-negative dynamin/shiTS1 allele. When imaged under restrictive conditions, shi disruption decreased the frequency of actin patch dynamics (Figure 7D–E).
evidence: This is stated in the results and supported by patch frequency data in Figure 7D-E.

claim: The morphology and duration of synaptic actin patches are similar to WASp/Arp2/3-dependent endocytic actin dynamics in yeast (16 s).
source: The link between the actin structures that we observed and endocytic events is supported by several lines of evidence: the morphology and duration of synaptic actin patches are similar to WASp/Arp2/3-dependent endocytic actin dynamics in yeast (16 s; Berro and Pollard, 2014) and somewhat briefer than in cultured mammalian cells (~40 s; Grassart et al., 2014; Merrifield et al., 2004; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The morphology and duration of synaptic actin patches are somewhat briefer than in cultured mammalian cells (~40 s).
source: The link between the actin structures that we observed and endocytic events is supported by several lines of evidence: the morphology and duration of synaptic actin patches are similar to WASp/Arp2/3-dependent endocytic actin dynamics in yeast (16 s; Berro and Pollard, 2014) and somewhat briefer than in cultured mammalian cells (~40 s; Grassart et al., 2014; Merrifield et al., 2004; Taylor et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The time constant for endocytosis at the Drosophila NMJ is ~14 s.
source: Given the measured time constant for endocytosis (~14 s; Poskanzer et al., 2006) and clathrin dependence of vesicle cycling in this synapse (Heerssen et al., 2008), these values support the hypothesis that synaptic actin patches are likely sites of clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: Vesicle cycling at the Drosophila NMJ is clathrin dependent.
source: Given the measured time constant for endocytosis (~14 s; Poskanzer et al., 2006) and clathrin dependence of vesicle cycling in this synapse (Heerssen et al., 2008), these values support the hypothesis that synaptic actin patches are likely sites of clathrin-mediated endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.

claim: The frequency of patch assembly approaches the rate of spontaneous synaptic vesicle release at the Drosophila NMJ (~5–6/10 μm2/min).
source: Further, the frequency of patch assembly, which we measured in resting synapses, approaches the rate of spontaneous synaptic vesicle release at this synapse (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B, Figure 1—figure supplement 2A) (~5–6/10 μm2/min; Melom et al., 2013; Akbergenova et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations and data references.

claim: Much of the membrane-remodeling machinery is likely held in an inactive state at the presynaptic membrane.
source: Our data indicate that much of this membrane-remodeling machinery is likely held in an inactive state at the presynaptic membrane: Nwk and Dap160 accumulate in a micron-scale membrane domain (Figure 2), and their loss increases the frequency of short-lived actin patches (Figure 6).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the experimental data.

claim: PAZ proteins are held in a partially autoinhibited state at the membrane in vivo.
source: These data suggest that these PAZ proteins are held in a partially autoinhibited state at the membrane in vivo, consistent with our prior in vitro observations (Stanishneva-Konovalova et al., 2016).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: Most Clc and AP2 puncta at the synapse are either not stabilized to form productive endocytic sites or associated with some non-endocytic functions.
source: This is further consistent with the broad distribution of Clc and AP2 to the membrane (Figure 7, Figure 7—figure supplement 1). Given the comparatively low rate of endocytosis expected at rest at this synapse, this suggests that most Clc and AP2 puncta at the synapse are either not stabilized to form productive endocytic sites (Aguet et al., 2013) or associated with some non-endocytic functions (Gimber et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the data.

claim: The actin structures assembled in the nwk mutant are unproductive for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
source: The fact that loss of Nwk increases the frequency of patches while decreasing FM uptake suggests that the actin structures assembled in the nwk mutant are unproductive for synaptic vesicle endocytosis.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an inference from the combined patch frequency and FM uptake data.

claim: Additional WASp activators such as Snx9 and Cip4/Toca-1 may play accessory roles in endocytic actin assembly.
source: Indeed, additional WASp activators such as Snx9 and Cip4/Toca-1 may play accessory roles in endocytic actin assembly (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018; Gallop et al., 2013), consistent with our finding that loss of presynaptic WASp leads to a decrease in the total number of patches (Figure 1G–I, Figure 1—figure supplement 1C–E).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations and data references.

claim: In human cells, the interaction between FCHSD2, intersectin, and WASp promotes actin assembly and endocytic maturation or initiation.
source: Similarly, in human cells, the interaction between FCHSD2, intersectin, and WASp promotes actin assembly and endocytic maturation (Almeida-Souza et al., 2018) or initiation (Xiao et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with supporting citations.

claim: The endocytic machinery can be deployed as clamped, primed, or activated complexes at different locations at the synapse.
source: Our data suggest that the endocytic machinery can be deployed as clamped, primed, or activated complexes at different locations at the synapse.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as a conclusion from the experimental findings.

claim: Nwk autoinhibition provides a mechanism to assemble an inactive, yet poised endocytic apparatus.
source: Our findings on autoinhibition and clamping connect two prevailing models of the organization and function of the synaptic endocytosis machinery—preassembly and delivery. In the first model, preassembly of clathrin and accessory proteins is hypothesized to ensure fast endocytosis in response to synaptic vesicle fusion (Hua et al., 2011; Mueller et al., 2004; Wienisch and Klingauf, 2006). Here, Nwk autoinhibition provides a mechanism to assemble an inactive, yet poised endocytic apparatus.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion as an interpretation of the findings.

claim: Dap160/intersectin can shuttle between the synaptic vesicle pool and the plasma membrane.
source: Because Dap160/intersectin can shuttle between the synaptic vesicle pool and the plasma membrane, is itself subject to autoregulation (Gerth et al., 2017), and can regulate other endocytic proteins (e.g., dynamin, Nwk), it could serve as a single activator that couples the preassembly and delivery models.
evidence: This is stated in the discussion with a supporting citation.
